A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Proxy-GS work. All 14 pages of each version, including the supplementary material, are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original rendering-quality and speed experiments, component ablations, runtime analyses and proxy-fidelity tests in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments, including benchmark comparisons in Tables 1–2 and supplementary results in Tables 6–10.

M1.justification: Proxy construction, hardware depth rendering, visibility filtering and proxy-guided densification remain unchanged in Sections 4.2–4.3 and the appendix. The added sky-region example illustrates the existing invalid-depth rule without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five MatrixCity blocks, real-world Small City streets, Berlin indoor scene and CUHK-LOWER aerial scene. No dataset, task or evaluated environmental condition is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain 3DGS, Scaffold-GS, Hierarchical-GS and its threshold variants, and Octree-GS. The FlashGS and Hardware 3DGS renderer comparisons and the nvdiffrast/3DGS depth-source comparisons also retain identical comparator membership.

E3.justification: The MatrixCity partitions, 40k-iteration training budget, baseline thresholds, voxel size, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/FPS metrics and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. The appendix retains the same proxy perturbations and safety-margin settings.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same training-component ablation, runtime breakdown, renderer integrations, proxy-resolution/noise tests and safety-margin analysis. The vertex-noise visualization and its explanation move from Section 5.2/Figure 6 in v3 to Appendix 8.5/Figure 8 in v5; they are not new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Averaging across scenes or blocks remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All ten tables retain identical values, and the plots and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Proxy-GS retains 21.68 PSNR and 151 FPS on MatrixCity Block 5 in Table 1, and 23.09 PSNR and 139 FPS on Small City in Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 and the unnumbered densification equations are unchanged, including the appendix's mesh-simplification and conservative visibility derivations. No mathematical assumption, theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The second introduction contribution explicitly adds that Proxy-GS introduces virtually no overhead in scenes with few occlusions. The principal claims about proxy-guided training, rendering quality, speedups and sub-millisecond depth acquisition remain unchanged in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: The explanations of scene-dependent gains, geometry-aligned densification, mesh-noise sensitivity and safety-margin tradeoffs remain substantively unchanged. The explanation of noise-induced ground artifacts is relocated to Appendix 8.5 without adding a new limitation or mechanism.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same hyperparameters, A100 training and RTX 4090 inference hardware, mesh-extraction workflows, and Vulkan–CUDA/PyTorch interoperability details. Naming the existing dataset and clarifying hardware-depth wording add no substantive reproducibility information or access instructions.

R1.justification: v5 adds GauHuman, Holi-Spatial, SpatialLM and Visionary, expanding the application context and adding a short WebGPU/browser-rendering discussion. It also rephrases the occlusion limitation of prior LOD approaches. Publication and title updates for retained references do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: v5 makes limited wording clarifications, updates affiliations, adds an acknowledgment and introduces an appendix heading for the relocated vertex-noise discussion. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain unchanged; the revised introductory LOD sentence introduces awkward grammar.

P2.justification: The vertex-noise visualization moves to the appendix, with associated figure renumbering; the framework figure, renderer table and mesh visualization also shift position. Figure 4 relabels the same displayed scene from BLOCK 0 to BLOCK 1. The displays otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added related-work context, explicit low-occlusion claim and small labeling clarifications provide limited editorial benefits. These coexist with awkward revised wording and an abstract that now spills onto the next page. With the scientific evidence, analysis and reproducibility information preserved, the changes establish no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
